split_why: Four days in Chiang Mai first, because its best things are all on dry land (the elephant sanctuary, temples, the Saturday and Sunday walking streets, a farm cooking class, ziplining and a jungle coaster), so the no-swim rule for 25 to 28 Dec costs nothing. Then four days in Bangkok for Muay Thai, the Dream World theme park, the Grand Palace, the floating and railway markets and the ICONSIAM countdown, Thailand’s biggest New Year’s Eve. There are no beach days: a Krabi or Phuket hop would add a flight and a hotel change for one beach day, so the plan spends the days on the cities instead. Open-jaw flights (in to Chiang Mai, home from Bangkok) and one short domestic flight keep it simple.
monkeys_note: Chiang Mai and Bangkok have no macaque spots on this plan. The plan skips Lopburi’s monkey temple, the Chiang Mai monkey shows and Krabi’s Tiger Cave Temple, and the Doi Suthep visit stays at the temple terrace.

route: Hanoi 4 days, Ho Chi Minh City 4 days
split_why: Four days in Hanoi cover the Old Quarter street food, Ha Long Bay and Ninh Binh while the north is cool and dry, so days 1 to 4 need no swimming anyway. One two-hour flight then moves to Ho Chi Minh City for four warm days with a hotel pool from day 5, the Cu Chi Tunnels, go-karts, the Mekong Delta and the country’s biggest New Year’s Eve countdown on Nguyen Hue. Open-jaw flights (in to Hanoi, home from Ho Chi Minh City) avoid any backtracking.
monkeys_note: The plan skips Monkey Island near Cat Ba and the Lan Ha Bay tours that stop there, and picks a Ha Long Bay route via Sung Sot Cave and Ti Top Island; wild macaques are sometimes seen on the cliffs at Luon Cave, so keep food out of sight on the kayak or bamboo boat. Ho Chi Minh City’s Can Gio Monkey Island is also left out.

split_why: Four days in Penang give George Town’s street food, street art and heritage houses, a Nyonya cooking class, Penang Hill and the ESCAPE adventure park, all on dry land for the no-swim days 1 to 4. Four days in Kuala Lumpur hold the Genting SkyWorlds theme park day trip, the Petronas Towers, the country’s biggest New Year’s Eve countdown at KLCC and a rafting day. Open-jaw flights (in to Penang, home from Kuala Lumpur) and one 1-hour domestic flight keep travel short.
monkeys_note: Skips the known macaque spots: Batu Caves, Penang Botanic Gardens, Penang National Park (Monkey Beach) and The Habitat forest trail on Penang Hill. On Penang Hill the plan keeps to the funicular, the viewpoints and the restaurant; leaf monkeys may be seen in the trees, and macaques sometimes come near the upper station, so keep food packed away.

route: Bohol 3 days, Cebu 2 days, Manila 3 days
split_why: Three days in Bohol for the Chocolate Hills, the tarsiers, the Loboc River and the Danao canyon swing, all on land (no swimming on days 1 to 4); two days in Cebu for the old city and, on day 5, the one swim day with the Moalboal sardines and Kawasan canyoneering; three days in Manila last for Binondo, Intramuros and the country’s biggest New Year’s Eve countdown in Bonifacio Global City. Cairo–Manila return flights, one domestic flight in, a ferry Bohol to Cebu and one flight back to Manila.
monkeys_note: Monkeys are not a real issue on this route. The tarsiers at the Corella sanctuary are tiny protected primates seen quietly on branches, not food-grabbing monkeys. Long-tailed macaques live in some Bohol forests and are sometimes kept as roadside photo props, so the plan skips any stop that offers monkey photos and takes no food out at the Bilar forest; none are reported at Danao, Cebu City, Kawasan, Moalboal or Manila.

split_why: Five days in Tokyo cover the city sights, both teamLab museums, a street go-kart ride, a sushi class and a full day at Tokyo DisneySea on a Monday, when the park is a little quieter than at the weekend. On 30 Dec the Shinkansen stops in Kyoto for the day on the way to Osaka. Osaka comes last so New Year’s Eve is the Universal Studios Japan countdown party, whose pass also lets you back into the park on 1 Jan for Super Nintendo World. Open-jaw flights (in to Tokyo, home from Osaka Kansai) mean no backtracking.
monkeys_note: Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka city areas have no wild monkeys that visitors meet. The plan avoids the Arashiyama monkey park in Kyoto.

route: Beijing 3 days, Zhangjiajie 2 days, Shanghai 3 days
split_why: Three days in Beijing cover the pandas at Beijing Zoo, Universal, the Forbidden City and the Great Wall with toboggan; two days in Zhangjiajie give one afternoon for Tianmen Mountain and one full day in the Avatar mountains; three days in Shanghai put Disneyland and the New Year’s Eve countdown at the end. Open-jaw flights (in to Beijing, home from Shanghai) and two direct domestic flights keep it simple.
monkeys_note: Wild macaques live in the Zhangjiajie forest (Yuanjiajie and the Golden Whip Stream trail are known for them), so the plan keeps to the Bailong elevator, Tianzi Mountain cable car and viewpoints, takes no food out in the open and skips the Golden Whip Stream walk. Beijing and Shanghai have none that visitors meet.

split_why: The same Tokyo–Osaka plan moved to the cheapest week of November 2026 (fly out Mon 2 Nov, days 1 to 8 Tue 3 to Tue 10 Nov, fly home Wed 11 Nov), chosen because DisneySea on Fri 6 Nov is in the lowest ¥9,900 price tier, Universal Studios Japan on Mon 9 and Tue 10 Nov falls on quiet weekdays, Cross Hotel Osaka is at its cheapest from Sunday to Tuesday nights, the Osaka–Cairo flight on 11 Nov is the cheapest of the month, and the week is well before the late-November autumn-leaves peak and the 21 to 23 Nov holiday weekend.
monkeys_note: Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka city areas have no wild monkeys that visitors meet. The plan avoids the Arashiyama monkey park in Kyoto.

reason: Little variety without water activities: no karting or rafting, and most highlights are boat or snorkel trips
split_why: Without snorkelling, diving and repeated boat trips, Maafushi has about four distinct days, so one night moves to the resort, which also cuts mosquito exposure on the local island and adds the resort’s free festive events, at a higher cost.
monkeys_note: There are no monkeys anywhere in the Maldives; the only wildlife in this plan is dolphins seen from a boat.
Red colobus monkeys in Jozani Forest, which you can skip, and Sykes’ monkeys in some beach-hotel gardens. Stone Town has none.
Toque macaques and langurs are common in south-coast gardens, on hotel roofs and along the Bentota river.

reason: Mostly romantic, too few activities, shopping no different from Egypt
monkeys_note: Long-tailed macaques live in the forests and gorges and sometimes visit hotel gardens near them; beach areas see few.

reason: Not your style; replaced by the southern Vietnam route
monkeys_note: Few wild monkeys; mostly at the safari park, which you can skip.
